requirements.statement: Per normal run, the added writer work of all RS-B register transactions (reserve, arm, bind, commit, reservation release, including the reservation/hold JOIN inside _release_obligation) plus the commit cost the register rows add plus the memory-hold transactions is under 5 ms in total, measured on the real operations (one warm-up run, then the median of five).

One eligible unarmed lease behind 128 blocked (live) leases, with 50 new blocked arrivals before every batch, is released within 4 start-pass batches, at most 64 released per batch, the median wall-clock of each batch position under 50 ms over repeated runs; the pass does equal SQLite work with and without released lease history. This is the observable budget; the section 5 mechanism is RS-B-9-B6-MECH.
The start pass's work is flat as released history grows (small scale in the suite; 100,000 released leases and reservations in scripts/measure_s13.py).

1,000 due holds drain, at the start pass's own batch size of 64 (direct calls, scheduling excluded), within ceil((1000+64)/64)+1 = 18 batches, at most 64 released per batch, each batch under 50 ms (median of three repeats) and in total under 60 s. The production path is RS-10-DUE-PROD.
RS-B draft 4 section 5 (bounded selection, back-off, re-due order): a start-pass batch selects at most 64 rows and a blocked row gets a back-off so later batches do not examine it before it is due.

1,000 due holds are released within 60 s by the service's own maintenance cadence (driver _expire_results every 10 s, writer expire pass, lease pass limit=10). FINDING: NOT MET by the product (100 passes, about 990 s; 60 released by 60 s). The test pins the measured miss until the proposed step lands.

Regression controls: patching the product in the test only, to release 128 rows per call or to slow the reservation/hold JOIN by 6 ms, turns the per-batch and B1 checks red; the mechanism check is red for an unbounded selection or a missing back-off; a pass that drains everything clears the production finding.
